 ### Sample

 User Story Definition and Components

A user story represents a piece of business value deliverable within a sprint, describing who needs it, what they need, and why they need it.
Good user stories include a clear description of the business value, assumptions or details relevant to development, and acceptance criteria defining when the story is done.
Acceptance Criteria and Gherkin Syntax

Acceptance criteria specify the definition of done to avoid misunderstandings about story completion.
The Gherkin syntax ("Given, When, Then") is used to clearly describe the preconditions, actions, and expected outcomes for the story.
INVEST Acronym for Good Stories

User stories should be Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable to ensure they are manageable and meaningful.
Stories that are too large to fit in a sprint are broken down or classified as Epics.
Epics and Their Use

Epics are large user stories that span multiple sprints and are broken down into smaller stories for sprint planning.
They capture big ideas or features that require decomposition into manageable parts for development.
